name: Use the canonical catalog language from the context documents
description: The domain vocabulary lives in CONTEXT-MAP.md (the list of contexts and how they relate) and docs/contexts/<context>/CONTEXT.md (one glossary per context). Catalog and Inventory are written; the others are added when their first seed starts. Use these terms exactly, and check the glossary before adding a synonym or moving a term between contexts. Maintain the files with the domain-modeling skill (~/.agents/skills/domain-modeling): a CONTEXT.md is a glossary only, with 1–2 sentence definitions and an Avoid list, and terms are written down as soon as they are resolved. docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md was never committed and is unavailable.

title: Use immutable full Part Revision snapshots and optimistic commands
rationale: Semantic edits publish immutable full snapshots grouped by a reasoned Change Set. Commands carry the expected head, restores create successor revisions, and no-op changes are rejected. Supplier prices, inventory, scans, and drafts are operational facts and do not create Part Revisions.

title: Separate logical assets, stored bytes, and semantic revisions
rationale: Asset ID is long-lived logical identity, blob SHA-256 content-addresses exact bytes, and revision snapshot hash identifies the full semantic and legal declaration. Provenance and license declarations attach to exact Asset Revisions. Moving or replicating a blob does not create a revision.

title: Treat qualification and Engineering Protection as orthogonal
rationale: Qualification is immutable evidence about an exact revision. Engineering Protection is an auditable mutation policy on a logical Managed Part or Asset. The permitted repair path is explicit unprotect with reason, revise, verify or qualify, and protect the new head; authority never becomes an invisible edit bypass.

name: Binary-safe content addressing inside PocketBase hooks
description: $security.sha256 hashes text, so bytes that are not UTF-8 would hash wrongly. The catalog import sends blobs as base64 in the JSON command and infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_lib.js decodes and hashes them in pure JS (checked against Node crypto) before $filesystem.fileFromBytes, so blobs are verified and written in the same transaction. Canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (snapshots, declarations) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler.

title: Derive Catalog record IDs from content and diff legacy imports server-side
rationale: Every Catalog record ID is the first 15 hex digits of SHA-256('kicad-parts:<kind>:v1\n<key>') (Managed Part from IPN, Asset from kind+LIB:NAME, Asset Revision from asset+revision hash, Blob from bytes hash, Change Set from correlation ID), computed in crates/catalog/src/ids.rs and re-derived by the route, so re-imports resolve to the same records without a mapping table. A symbol's Asset Blob is the exact byte span of that one top-level symbol (Provenance keeps file path, file hash and byte range), so editing a neighbouring symbol does not revise it; footprints and 3D models are whole files. POST /api/catalog/legacy-imports diffs against stored state in one transaction: nothing new is a 422 no-op with no Change Set; a changed snapshot gets a successor only when the head's Change Set kind is legacy-import, otherwise an Import Diagnostic; a changed row with an unchanged snapshot (an Operational Fact) is kept as an Import Diagnostic. Supplier PNs, LCSC and prices stay in Part Revision Provenance, never in the snapshot.
